title: attention-tiler buffer reuse + scheduling skew causing softmax-instability and token misordering
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A correctness regression was observed after recent attention tiler and scheduler refactors. Under mid-to-long sequence workloads with mixed-precision kernels and asynchronous prefill/decode scheduling, we see sporadic numerical instability in the attention softmax (NaNs or large probability spikes) and occasional token reordering or dropped tokens. The bug appears in the runtime path that reuses tiler buffers across simultaneous prefill and decode lanes when kernel-selection switches between quantized and FP16 variants. Impact: customer-facing UIs report hallucinated scores and a subset of requests show token skips or out-of-order tokens, primarily for sequences >1024 tokens and batch sizes >=8. Repro rate in our synthetic harness ~1-3% for affected traces but higher in some customer workloads. This is a high-severity correctness issue that regresses output fidelity.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Initial report from QA after staged rollout of attn-tiler refactor. Attached failing trace and minimal repro harness. Marking as P0 because outputs diverge from baseline and some requests produce NaNs.

2026-03-02 - Liam Chen: Reproduced locally against fc6e1b8 with long-seq stress runner. Observed NaN when tiler buffer offset reused across prefill and decode lanes where kernel selection toggles between quantized and fp16. Suspect stale metadata (tile stride / max_seq) not updated atomically during kernel swap.

2026-03-03 - Maria Gomez (Performance): Provided microbench showing that the new tiler rebalancer reassigns buffer ownership without a memory fence; this is safe for throughput but can race with an in-flight decode write completing. Added instrumentation to count buffer-handoffs.

2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Narrowed root cause to two cooperating races: (1) buffer metadata update not atomic with scheduler handoff, (2) kernel-selection cache (per-stream knob) uses relaxed synchronization so new kernel assumes tile stride semantics that don't match the current buffer layout. Together these cause mis-indexed softmax inputs leading to overflow/NaN on fp16 and extreme logits on quantized kernels.

2026-03-05 - Sandeep Rao (QA): Added deterministic repro that increases failure rate by forcing context switches between prefill and decode threads. Shared repro script and short video demonstrating token permutation for a synthetic conversation.

2026-03-06 - Liam Chen: Created a fix branch that adds an ownership token on tiler buffers plus a lightweight RCU-style epoch bump when kernel-selection changes. Also added a defensive softmax clamp for fp16 to avoid NaN while bug is mitigated. Running multi-node stress for 48 hours.

2026-03-08 - Performance: Stress run shows 0 failures in 48h vs ~120 failures on master in same time window. Latency impact measured: median decode latency +3% under heavy load; peak tails unchanged. Preparing PR for review.

2026-03-09 - Design/PM: Noted that we should add a console alert when softmax-clamp is triggered to surface quality mitigation to customers. PM requested flag to gate the epoch-based fix behind an experiment for safest rollout.

2026-03-10 - Liam Chen: Opened PR #12842 (WIP) with tests, instrumentation, and migration plan. Coordinating canary rollout on dedicated pools and adding additional unit tests for kernel-selection transitions. Blocking follow-ups: API to expose per-stream kernel metadata and small refactor of scheduler to read ephemeral flags atomically.
